In 1902 the new Australian parliament, then sitting in Melbourne, passed a law giving most women the vote in federal elections and the right to stand for parliament. Australia was among the first nations to do both.

South Australia had led the way in 1895. Campaigners such as Vida Goldstein and Catherine Helen Spence pushed the cause, nine years after New Zealand.

The same law shut out most Aboriginal people, men and women, who gained the federal vote only in 1962. The first women entered federal parliament in 1943. See Federation and 1967 referendum.
